summary: A search of one folder (Search Only in "Folder name", Smart Folders with a folder, the file chooser, `--here`, and `fff find` / `fff search` with `--scope` or `--here`) no longer writes the folder's glob into the text fff-search parses. In crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, `search_root` and `grep_cancellable` build the glob for every folder with a new private helper, `folder_glob(rel: &Path)`: each of `* ? [ ] { }` and `\` stands in a set of its own, the path's names are joined with `/`, and `/**` ends it. They hand it to fff-search as `Constraint::Glob` beside the constraints the parser returns: after each of the three parses in `search_root`, into `constraints` for several patterns, onto the parsed query for one pattern. The 20,000 over-fetch for specially named folders in `search_root` and the four-times page for names with a space in the grep loop are gone, and `page_end` is given `limit` again. For one pattern in a folder, `raw_query` is emptied, so fff-search's own root-wide second search cannot run. The engine makes that second search itself, for the whole pattern, in the folder only and in what is left of the time limit (`root_budget_ms`), never for a search that was told to stop, and the time limit is judged by the pass whose answer is kept. A pattern that is filters and nothing else is first looked for as text in the files its filters leave, as fff-search does where it is given no folder. A search of This Computer, of a whole search location, and of a folder outside the search locations (an index to itself, no glob) is made as before. Two source files changed: engine.rs, and one comment in `content_search` (src/finder/mod.rs). No documentation needed changing.
changelog: **Search Only in "Folder name"** gave wrong or missing results in a folder whose path has a space, a bracket, a brace, `*`, `?`, or `!` in it, such as `Tax Returns` or `photos[2024]`. A contents search there could say No Results while files in the folder matched, once enough newer files elsewhere had the word, and found nothing at all in a folder such as `drafts[old]`. A name search could miss the folder's items when more than 20,000 others matched better. On macOS and Linux, a folder with a backslash in its name could not be searched at all. A search of one folder now looks only at what is in that folder, whatever it is called. A contents search of a folder that finds nothing also no longer goes on to read the rest of the search location, which could take it to nearly twice the time limit, and it finds text that reads like a filter, such as `!important`, `*.rs`, or `src/`, as a search of This Computer does. A folder name typed alone, such as `src/`, lists only folders in a search of one folder too, and a file opened from such a search ranks higher the next time. `fff find` and `fff search` with `--scope` or `--here` follow the same rules; with `fff find --files`, a folder name alone is a word in a folder as it is elsewhere.
behaviour_changes: All of these are for searches of one folder that is inside a search location: Search Only in "Folder name" in the window, Smart Folders with a folder, the file chooser, `--here`, and `fff find` / `fff search` with `--scope` or `--here`. Searches of This Computer, of a whole search location and of a folder outside the search locations are unchanged: 756 name searches and 342 content searches with no folder gave the same answer on the trunk's engine and on this commit.

Contents search, folder with a space in its path: the folder's matching files are listed however many newer files elsewhere have the word. Before, once more than four times (Results shown + 1) newer matching files existed elsewhere in the search location, the window said No Results over "0+ items". Seen in review with 2,100 newer matching files beside `Tax Returns`: No Results and "0+ items" on the trunk's engine, the folder's 4 files and "4 items" on this commit (pictures review-before-space, review-after-space).

Contents search, folder with `[`, `]`, `{` or `}` in its path and no space, such as `drafts[old]`: finds the folder's files. Before it found nothing at all, "0 items" (pictures review-before-brackets, review-after-brackets).

macOS and Linux, folder with a backslash in its name: name and contents searches of it work; before both found nothing. A folder with `*` or `?` in its name no longer has lookalike folders searched along with it.

Name search, folder with a space or any of `* ? [ ] { } !` in its path: the folder's matches are found even when more than 20,000 items elsewhere in the search location match better. Before, the list came out empty with no `+`. By reading, not run with that many files: a one-letter search there now takes the folder's own most used items, where it took the folder's share of the 20,000 most used items of the whole search location.

A contents search of a folder that finds nothing ends once the folder's files are read. Before, in every plainly named folder, it went on to read the whole search location for the search's text with the glob after it, for up to a second full time limit. Measured in review under a limit of 1 s (fuzzy mode, 64 files of 1.4 MB in the folder, 160 outside, a busy machine): 1.2 to 1.4 s on the trunk's engine, 0.2 to 0.5 s on this commit.

Contents search of a folder for text that reads as a filter (`!important`, `*.rs`, `src/`, `{a,b}`, `type:rust`), or with one beside words (`and *.rs`, `see src/`): found as a search of This Computer finds it; before, nothing was found in plainly named folders (picture review-after-filter-text). Of 5,130 content searches compared in review between the trunk's engine and this commit (14 folders and no folder, 38 patterns, plain, regex and fuzzy, three limits), none lost a line it had. In plainly named folders the only ones that changed are those with such a pattern.

When that second search runs out of time, the search counts as stopped ("stopped at the time limit", or Nothing Found Before the Time Limit with nothing found). Before, it said No Results after up to twice the limit. Measured: `qqqzzzxxx !skip` in the folder took 1.2 to 1.4 s and wasn't reported as stopped on the trunk's engine; 0.6 to 1.05 s on this commit, reported as stopped when the second search was cut short.

Name search with Any Kind in a plainly named folder: a search made of nothing but folder names (`src/`, `/notes/`, `archive/old/`, `!src/`, `notes/ !src/`, a lone `/`) lists folders only, as it does in a search of This Computer, as it already did in specially named folders, and as the manual says of `src/`. Before, it listed files too (pictures review-before-folder-word: 11 items, review-after-folder-word: 3 folders). This is the one change where a search lists less than it did: `!src/` typed alone listed every file outside `src` and now lists the folders outside it.

`fff find --files` with `--scope` or `--here` and a lone folder name: it is a fuzzy word, as without a folder. Before, it was an exact folder filter: `src/` listed the two files in `src`, and now lists them first and loose matches after them.

`fff search --scope/--here` with several patterns: each pattern is read by itself, so `src/` as the first of several is text. Before, the first pattern was read together with the glob, which made a filter of it.

A file opened from a search of a plainly named folder ranks higher the next time for the same words. Before, folder searches there got no such boost, because the text the search was looked up under had the glob in it.
A sort that chooses a cut list's items chooses among up to 20,000 matches inside a specially named folder, where it chose among 20,000 of the whole search location. Not tested by itself.

Engine counts that nothing shows: `SearchResponse.total_matched`, `GrepResponse.files_with_matches` and `files_searched` count only the folder for specially named folders, and `files_searched` is the second search's count when one was made.

Apart from the folder-name-only searches above, name searches of a folder list what they did: of 11,340 compared in review between the trunk's engine and this commit (14 folders and no folder, 63 queries, Any Kind with and without folders, Folder, Document, Code, Image, with and without a sort), the items and scores are the same everywhere but for those searches in the four plainly named folders (90) and for the folder with a backslash, where the trunk found nothing.
left_out: No automated test for the time handling of the second search (its budget from what is left, `stopped` when none is left, the limit judged by the kept pass): it needs real seconds. Measured by hand by the implementer and again in review (behaviour_changes).

No test that a folder search with no filter in it that finds nothing reads the folder once: removing `!filtered` from the condition makes the same search twice with the same answer, so only the time tells (the thirteenth mutation in notes).

A search of This Computer, of a whole search location, and of a folder outside the search locations is made as before, as the plan says. fff-search's own second search still runs there for a pattern with a filter that finds nothing, with a second full time budget: `qqqzzzxxx !skip` with no folder took 1.5 to 1.9 s under a 1 s limit on both engines, and when the first search ended inside the limit nothing said it stopped.
CHANGELOG.md: the guide forbids it; the entry is in the commit message.

docs/manual.md, README.md, docs/protocol.md and the Search Syntax dialog are unchanged. Read in review: the Toolbar row and the scope bar table, Search syntax and the paragraphs under it, Ranking and limits, the messages table, the time-limit row, the Nushell command table and protocol.md's `scope` and `pattern` rows. None states what changed. The manual's sentence that with Any Kind a folder filter that is the whole search finds the folders that match it is now true in a folder search too.
Folder names that aren't UTF-8 still cannot be searched as one folder (to_string_lossy), as before.
The lossy `Tax*Returns*2024*/**` helper and PathSegment were not used, as the verifier decided.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: src/term, src/macos.rs and src/win.rs call none of the engine's search functions (grepped), and the new names are private to engine.rs.
Not compiled or run for macOS or Windows.

notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit 5ebf1cf: 591 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. The trunk moved by two commits during the review (e746db6 quick-look-window-mixup, c27b4b5 menu-bar-mac-keys). The rebase was clean, neither touches the engine, content_search or the scope tests, and the check ran on the final commit. Pushed to origin (c27b4b5..5ebf1cf). The commit on the trunk has the implementer's code and tests line for line; only its message differs (review_fixes).

How it was checked.
(1) Tests without the change. The trunk's engine code above `mod tests`, under this commit's test module, with a stand-in for `folder_glob` so that the helper's test compiles. Seven of the eight new or changed engine tests fail, each for its reason: content crowding 0 hits for 3; name crowding [] for ["n-e-e-d-l-e.txt"]; special names total_matched 14 for 1; the trap ([], 1) for ([], 0); the stop test at its first assertion, 0 hits for 1; remembers README.md for readme.md; the lone `archive/` not folders only. The eighth is the helper's own test, which passes on the stand-in, and searches_a_folder passes as it should. On the same code the finder unit test fails with 0 rows for 2 and the UI test with [] for the two files of `Tax Returns`. The lane was clean again after each.
(2) Thirteen one-line mutations of the final code, each run against the engine's tests: no escaping in folder_glob; the backslash not escaped; raw_query not emptied; the second search keeping the pattern's filters; a stopped search made again; a pattern of filters alone not given as text; no glob in each of the three name-search branches; no glob for several patterns; no second search; no glob for one pattern. Each of these twelve fails at least one test, and without the escaping the UI test fails at `drafts[old]`. The thirteenth passes: a second search made when the pattern had no filter (`!filtered` removed) repeats the first with the same answer, so only the time tells (left_out).
(3) Trunk against commit. A probe (an integration test in crates/fffinder-core/tests, removed again) on a copy of the demo folder with fifteen folders of the same fifteen files added: `plain`, `Tax Returns`, `drafts[old]`, `My Docs [old]`, `x{a,b}`, `!new`, `q*r?`, `back\slash`, `deep/in side/the [tree]`, and a lookalike beside each (382 files, search.threads = 1; two runs of each engine gave the same 32,940 lines). 11,340 name searches and 5,130 content searches, each compared between the trunk's engine and this commit; behaviour_changes has what came out. With no folder nothing differs. No content search lost a line. In the four plainly named folders the name searches that differ are the ones made of folder names only: 90 of 3,024.
(4) In place against alone. 4,455 content searches (nine folders, 55 patterns, three modes, three limits), each made of the folder inside the big search location and of an engine whose only search location is that folder. 3,777 agree in lines, `more`, `stopped` and both counts. 588 differ in `files_searched` alone: the engine keeps the second search's count, where fff-search keeps the first's when its second finds nothing. 90 differ in lines, all for a pattern with a filter that names a path (`invoice src/**`, `TODO notes/`), which is read from the search location down, as the manual says.
(5) Odd names. 81 folders (`a,b`, `[!x]`, `[^x]`, `]`, `}{`, `**`, `\`, `a\`, `[]]`, a newline, a tab, a no-break space, accents in both forms, an emoji, quotes, `type:rust`, `*.rs`, `!*.rs`, `q*r?/**/z`, `x/[y]/{z}/w*v` and more), each with a file and a subfolder with a file. Four kinds of name search and five content searches of each: on this commit every one lists exactly the folder's own, but for two dot-folders, which the index doesn't hold (Found, not fixed). On the trunk's engine 174 of the 729 checks fail.
(6) Time, by hand, under a limit of 1 s; the figures are in behaviour_changes and left_out. The fixture (300 MB) is deleted.
(7) Nine pictures of my own (review-*), taken in a copy of the demo folder with `Tax Returns` (4 files with the word, an hour old), `drafts[old]` (2), 2,100 newer files with the word in `Ledger/2024`, and two style sheets with `!important`. The before pictures are from the lane with the trunk's engine.rs.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code and the runs say.
(1) A folder search that lists nothing, or less than it did, with nothing to say why. The glob has to match exactly what fff-search holds for the folder. globset reads `? * [ { } , \` specially outside a set and nothing but `]`, `-`, a leading `!` or `^` inside one; folder_glob sets each of `* ? [ ] { } \` alone in a set, a comma is plain once no brace is open, and a set of one character cannot fail to compile. On Windows `Path` splits at both separators, so no backslash is emitted there. Runs (3) and (5) found no folder whose own items a search missed. What a search of a folder does list less of: a search made of folder names only (behaviour_changes), which the plan accepted for `src/`.
(2) A contents search that takes longer, or says the wrong thing about how it ended. The second search is made only when the pattern had a filter, the first search read every file and found nothing, the search wasn't told to stop, and time is left; it gets what is left, and `stopped` comes from the search whose answer is kept. With no limit set, root_budget_ms gives 0, which is no limit to fff-search either, and out_of_time is false. `more` is now about the folder's own files: "0+ items" over No Results cannot come from a folder search any more.
(3) Something from outside the folder, or another order of results. The prefix checks stay in both functions. The trap test holds the empty raw_query, and run (4) found no line from outside. Scores are the same as on the trunk for every search in run (3) that lists the same items. The one thing that moves a result is the boost for a file opened from the same words, which the manual promises and which folder searches with plain names didn't get.

Doubts for the owner.
1. Only Linux was built and run. On Windows, folder_glob relies on `Path` splitting at `\`, and the new tests know a hit by the end of its path because the temporary folder is spelled another way in hit paths there and on macOS; I read both paths through and could not run them.
2. a_folder_with_a_space_in_its_name_isnt_crowded_out_of_a_name_search writes 21,000 empty files. It takes under half a second here, more on a loaded machine, and I can't tell for Windows CI. It is the only test of what a user sees of the name-search half. The `total_matched == 1` assertions of the special-names test also fail without the glob, so the big test can go if it proves too slow there.
3. `!src/` typed alone, and `notes/ !src/`, list folders only in every folder search now. In plainly named folders they listed files too, by accident of the glob standing at the end of the text. It is what This Computer does and what specially named folders did; I'd call the rule itself the bug (Found, not fixed).
4. `fff find --files --scope X src/` lists loose matches after the files in `src`, where it listed those two files alone.
5. A pattern that is only a `type:` token filters nothing in a content search, so it is searched twice, in a folder by the engine and elsewhere by fff-search. In a folder so large that one pass takes more than half the limit, the second runs out of time and the search says it stopped though every file was read once.
6. It rests on fff-search 0.11: a `Constraint::Glob` goes to globset as it is, an empty raw_query switches the second search off, and the flag is looked at only at every eighth file (the stop test needs that). If fff-search's zlob feature is ever turned on, the escaping has to be checked again.

For briefs still to come.
- query-history-boost: the scope part of your brief is done. `search_root` no longer writes the folder's glob into the text fff-search is given, so `raw_query` is the typed text and `kind_tokens`, and a_search_of_one_folder_remembers_what_it_opened (after a_search_with_a_folder_filter_remembers_what_it_opened) holds it for Any Kind. Still looked up under another text than `track_open` writes: a file kind (kind_tokens appended), a one-letter search (emptied), and a search whose slash-ending tokens were moved to the front. If you key by the typed text on both sides, the new test should pass as it is.
- regex-content-search: the loop in `grep_cancellable` now matches on `(patterns.as_slice(), scope_glob.as_deref())`. `([only], None)` is the old call. `([only], Some(glob))` builds the query you describe (raw_query empty, the glob pushed) and makes the second search itself. `(several, glob)` is multi_grep with the glob pushed. `scope_glob` is an `Option<String>` from the private helper `folder_glob(rel: &Path)` and has no space in front: `scope_glob.as_deref().map(Constraint::Glob)`, no trim_start. Put your Regex arm before the two `[only]` arms. Today a regex with a `*` and a `/` in it (`a.*b/c`) reads as a glob, in a folder as elsewhere: the first search finds nothing and the second looks for it as text. `options`, `budget_ms` and `root_started` are `mut`, because the second search resets them. `FuzzyQuery` is imported.
- search-settings-without-effect: `let mut options` in the grep loop, and the folder arm calls `picker.grep` twice with it. Your `allow_file_size` before `root.picker.read()` is not in the way. The deadline check still comes right after the lock.
- typo-fallback-near-miss: `scope_rel` is gone from `search_root`. The folder's glob is `scope_glob`, pushed as a constraint through `scope_filter` after each of the three parses and never appended to `query`. fff-search still matches words in the path from the search location down, so your "whole folder through the scope's own name" is as it was: in my probe `main` with Document lists all ten documents of a folder named `plain` or `Tax Returns`, as loose matches, and four of the same files in a folder named `!new`. A folder name typed alone in a folder search is folders only in every folder now, and still a loose word the strict check never sees: `src/` in the demo's Projects lists `atlas` and `beacon` beside `src` (picture review-after-folder-word).
- adhoc-index-feedback: a folder outside the search locations is the base of its own index and gets no glob, so its searches go through `([only], None)`, with fff-search's own second search and second time budget. If you let a subfolder use its parent's temporary index, it becomes a folder inside an index: it then gets the glob and the engine's second search with no more work, whatever it is called. The grep loop has no `page_limit` variable any more; the page is `limit`.
- result-tie-break: in a specially named folder fff-search is asked for `(limit * 4).max(2_000)` of the folder's own matches, as in any folder, not for 20,000 of the whole search location. `total_matched` counts the folder's own.
- empty-state-messages: a contents search of one folder no longer ends as "0+ items" over No Results. One with a filter in its pattern (`todo *.md`) that finds nothing can end as stopped, which shows Nothing Found Before the Time Limit, where it said No Results after up to twice the limit. `src/` typed in a folder that has no subfolders is No Results now in plainly named folders too.
- smart-folder-save-and-leaks: a Smart Folder saved with a folder and a search made of folder names only (`src/`, `notes/ !src/`) lists folders only from now on. One saved with Contents and text that reads as a filter (`!important`) finds what it says.
- content-match-highlight: in a folder search a hit's `ranges` come from whichever of the two searches is kept. From the second they cover the whole pattern, the filter-like token included. Nothing to handle.
- multi-word-highlights, live-search-results, recents-walk-index (all in engine.rs): new are `folder_glob` between `join_rel` and `fuzzy_text`, `scope_filter` and three `parsed.constraints.extend(scope_filter)` lines in `search_root` (each parse result is `let mut parsed`), and the match in the grep loop. Tests: one after a_search_with_a_folder_filter_remembers_what_it_opened, five after a_folder_with_a_space_in_its_name_isnt_crowded_out_of_a_content_search, one assertion in folder_filters_narrow_searches_that_can_list_folders. `highlight`, `rerank`, `recents` and `into_hit` are untouched.
- back-forward-restore-search, recent-searches, search-start-no-flash: in src/finder/mod.rs only a comment in `content_search` and the expectations of one unit test changed. tests/controls.rs has one new test, after search_scope_button.
- Whoever assembles CHANGELOG.md: the entry is the Changelog paragraph of the commit message, kind Fixed.

Found, not fixed (all on the trunk before this change).
- A contents search with no folder (This Computer, a whole search location, a folder outside the search locations) whose pattern has a filter in it and finds nothing gets fff-search's second search with a second full time budget. When the first search ends inside the limit and the second runs over it, nothing says the search stopped: 1.5 to 1.9 s under a limit of 1 s. The implementer found it. Sending `([only], None)` through the folder arm's code with no glob would cover it.
- With Any Kind, a search made of nothing but slash-ending tokens lists folders only: `!src/`, which reads as everything but `src`, and `notes/ !src/` list no files. fff-search searches folders only when the text it is given ends in a slash (file_picker.rs:1260), and the token sort in `search_root` only moves such tokens in front of others. It was so in This Computer and in specially named folders; this change makes plainly named folders the same.
- A folder name typed alone is matched loosely and never checked: `src/` lists `atlas` and `beacon` (the implementer's finding; typo-fallback-near-miss knows it).
- Search Only in a hidden folder finds nothing where the search location is not a git repository: fff-search doesn't index dot-folders or dot-files there, and a temporary index is only made for a folder outside every search location. Seen with `.hidden/needle.txt` and `seen/.inner/needle.txt`: the index lists `seen/needle.txt` alone, and both folder searches come back empty, by name and by contents, on the trunk's engine too.
- A pattern that is only a `type:` token is searched twice (doubt 5).

Housekeeping. My scratch folder (lane-b-scoped-search-special-folder-names in the shared scratchpad) is deleted, with the probe, its fixtures and the copy of the demo folder. The probe was a file in crates/fffinder-core/tests, removed again; the lane is clean and at the trunk's tip. Failing runs on the old code and under the mutations left 26 fixture folders in /tmp. I removed them one by one by name, after checking that each carried the process id and the time of one of my runs and that no such process was alive.
